mara.activity: Wake, wash up, take my prescription if due, and dress in comfortable clothes. I check that the relative has towels and water without disturbing them, then carry my phone downstairs.
mara.intention: Start gently and make sure the guest can manage the morning comfortably.

mara.activity: Make a simple breakfast for myself and set out fruit and water for the relative. I carry my plate and mug to the dining table, leaving the blue ceramic mug at the kitchen island afterward rather than risking it being used for anything else.
mara.intention: Feed myself and make hospitality easy without creating a formal breakfast obligation.

mara.activity: Do a small guest and downstairs reset: clear any obvious dishes, straighten the sofa, and check the bathroom supplies. I avoid starting a larger organizing project.
mara.intention: Make the shared rooms welcoming while keeping the disruption contained.

mara.activity: Have coffee, work through a crossword, and review the weekly calendar at the dining table. I make a short note about the relative's needs and leave the incoming mail stack undisturbed at the left end of the table.
mara.intention: Keep my usual planning anchor and identify only the household details that truly need attention.

mara.activity: Offer the relative tea or water and explain, lightly, where breakfast things are. I carry the tea to the living room if wanted, then give them room rather than filling the silence.
mara.intention: Anticipate needs without making the visit feel managed.

mara.activity: While Daniel handles his own late breakfast and kitchen cleanup, I take a quiet household-support interval: refresh the guest room and bathroom, replace a towel if needed, and put stray items back in their usual places.
mara.intention: Use Daniel's kitchen activity as a chance to prepare the rest of the house without directing him.

mara.activity: Sit with the relative for an easy conversation or shared reading, keeping the topic neutral when opinions become pointed. I bring my library book so I can read if the conversation pauses naturally.
mara.intention: Be affectionate and present while protecting a little mental space.

mara.activity: Prepare and serve a light lunch at the dining table using leftovers and fruit. I keep portions uncomplicated and carry used dishes to the kitchen when we finish.
mara.intention: Make lunch feel cared for without turning it into another production.

mara.activity: Wash the lunch dishes and wipe the kitchen counters, then place a small snack and fresh water where the relative can reach them. I leave Daniel alone if he is mentally occupied with work.
mara.intention: Reset the practical spaces and avoid adding conversation pressure.

mara.activity: Take a brief quiet pause in the bedroom with my phone and reading glasses, checking messages and making no new commitments. I listen for whether the relative needs anything, but do not hover.
mara.intention: Regain patience before the afternoon visit continues.

mara.activity: Give the relative a comfortable independent stretch while I sort a small amount of household paperwork at the dining table. I keep the mail stack intact and only note urgent follow-up items in my planner.
mara.intention: Create breathing room for everyone and prevent minor tasks from accumulating indefinitely.

mara.activity: Rejoin the relative in the living room with tea or water, then make space for Daniel to have a short quiet interval if he comes in distracted and does not want to talk. I do not ask him to explain the problem twice.
mara.intention: Welcome Daniel in doses and keep the emotional temperature low.

mara.activity: Wash the tea things and set out the cutting board, knives, and ingredients for the week's casserole. I check that the relative has a comfortable place to sit or read.
mara.intention: Transition into cooking without rushing or asking others to help.

mara.activity: Prepare vegetables and assemble a casserole for the coming week, following my usual Sunday routine. I keep the conversation optional, put the finished dish into the oven, and leave the counters reasonably clear.
mara.intention: Create dependable food for the week and give the household a useful, grounding rhythm.

mara.activity: Serve an easy dinner at the dining table, adding fruit or yogurt for the relative if useful. I keep the meal warm but do not insist that Daniel participate continuously if he is still mentally at work.
mara.intention: Offer shared time without making dinner another obligation.

mara.activity: Clear and wash the dinner things, wipe the kitchen, and put leftovers away. I carry a small glass of water and snack to the relative's usual resting place.
mara.intention: Prevent the evening from becoming visually crowded or logistically awkward.

mara.activity: Spend a low-key evening in the living room with the relative, offering tea and letting the television remain quiet or off. I read a few pages when conversation naturally pauses and give Daniel short stretches without questions.
mara.intention: Keep affection available while allowing everyone some recovery time.

mara.activity: Do a fast reset of the entry, sofa, and kitchen counters, then check that the relative has water, towels, and anything needed for the night. I put the tea things away but do not tackle the mail.
mara.intention: Reduce visual crowding and prevent tomorrow morning from starting awkwardly.

mara.activity: Wash up, change into pajamas, and bring my phone to the bedroom to charge. I make a brief planner note about the casserole and any guest follow-up, then set my reading glasses on the left nightstand.
mara.intention: Close the day deliberately and preserve my normal bedtime anchors.

mara.activity: Read quietly in bed, keeping the room calm while the relative settles elsewhere in the house. I turn out the light when I am sleepy.
mara.intention: End with restorative quiet rather than more conversation or tidying.

daniel.activity: Wake slowly, sit up, drink from the water bottle, and use the bathroom. Wash my hands and face, then return to the bedroom and check whether I feel steady enough for the day.
daniel.intention: Start cautiously while recovering and assess my energy before committing to the repair call.

daniel.activity: Take permitted morning medicine with water, get dressed in work trousers, a work shirt, socks, and work boots, and clip on my work belt and work keys. Put my wallet in my pocket and check that my phone is charged.
daniel.intention: Prepare for work without rushing or aggravating the cold.

daniel.activity: Go to the kitchen for a small breakfast. Carry a bowl and spoon to the counter, eat yogurt and a banana slowly, and drink water. Carry the empty bowl and spoon to the sink afterward.
daniel.intention: Have enough food before the long appointment without making myself nauseated.

daniel.activity: Make a modest pass at cleaning the kitchen: rinse the bowl and spoon, wipe the prep area, and leave the cleaning sponge and dish soap by the sink when finished. Refill the water bottle and bring it to my repair bag.
daniel.intention: Keep the usual Sunday kitchen routine, but stop before it becomes tiring.

daniel.activity: Greet the visiting relative warmly in the living room, answer a few questions, and explain that I need quiet breaks because I am still recovering. Check my appointment details and place the repair bag by the entry so I can leave cleanly.
daniel.intention: Be welcoming in a manageable dose and prevent awkwardness before work.

daniel.activity: Put on my jacket and work gloves, collect the repair bag and water bottle, and leave through the entry. Lock up and head to the repair call.
daniel.intention: Leave on time with the equipment and protective gear I need.

daniel.activity: Work the scheduled appliance repair, testing the machine methodically and checking the hidden fault with the multimeter and screwdriver set. Drink water during a short break and keep the customer updated without losing track of the symptoms.
daniel.intention: Find the real fault rather than leaving an unresolved repair.

daniel.activity: Eat the packed lunch at the service vehicle, then review the appliance symptoms in my pocket notebook. Call the customer back to answer one more question and decide what additional test or part is needed.
daniel.intention: Refuel and organize the problem while it is still fresh in my mind.

daniel.activity: Continue the repair after the hidden fault and the customer's additional questions extend the appointment. Test the machine again, explain the result, clean up my tools, and document the work before driving home.
daniel.intention: Finish responsibly even though the long call leaves me tired and keyed up.

daniel.activity: Return home, put the truck keys on the middle-right entry coat hook, and leave my work boots on the lower shoe-rack shelf. Carry the repair bag to the living room, wash my hands, and sit down for a few minutes before changing.
daniel.intention: Transition out of work without bringing the repair mess or outside germs through the house.

daniel.activity: Tell Mara the whole repair story while sitting on the sofa, including the hidden fault and what made the job run long. Drink water and accept a quiet pause if the relative joins the conversation.
daniel.intention: Share the responsibility I am replaying in my head without demanding a long evening of conversation.

daniel.activity: Eat a small portion of the casserole or vegetables Mara has prepared, carrying a plate and fork to the dining table with water. Carry the plate and fork to the kitchen sink afterward.
daniel.intention: Eat something restorative while keeping the meal modest because I am still recovering.

daniel.activity: Change out of my work shirt and trousers into an evening t-shirt and lounge shorts. Rest on the sofa with the throw blanket, using the remote for quiet television only if conversation gets tiring.
daniel.intention: Recover from the long appointment and take a brief stretch without conversation.

daniel.activity: Make a short call to my mother and sort the service receipt from today's job at the living-room coffee table. Write down the follow-up detail in my pocket notebook, then leave the notebook beside the phone rather than forcing more paperwork.
daniel.intention: Keep the usual Sunday call and receipt routine, shortened because work ran over.

daniel.activity: Take my temperature, drink water, and rest quietly while the relative and Mara manage their own evening conversation. Answer pleasantly if included, then close my eyes instead of trying to host continuously.
daniel.intention: Stay cordial while protecting the quiet recovery time I need.

daniel.activity: Wash my hands and face, brush my teeth, and take permitted evening medicine with water. Put the thermometer away and change into sleep pants and a sleep shirt.
daniel.intention: Complete the night routine and monitor whether the cold is worsening after the long workday.

daniel.activity: Put my wallet in the right nightstand drawer, set the water bottle, tissues, and phone beside the bed, and sleep under the quilt. Wake only for water, medicine if permitted, or the bathroom.
daniel.intention: Get a full night of recovery after the extended repair call.
